inputs.text: The High Court is right: suspicion is not evidence, and a phone contact with a Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri” cannot by itself justify prolonged detention. Invoking national security or the Official Secrets Act doesn’t make it acceptable to lock someone up when the state cannot establish a case. These powers can turn fear into punishment, with the accused forced to bear the cost of the state’s failure to prove its claims. Due process and liberty must protect everyone.
